question: How are the field lines inside the solenoid?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Parallel straight lines**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Straight parallel lines** make up the field lines on the inside of the **solenoid**.
 
• The **south pole** to the **north pole** inside the solenoid and the north pole to the south pole outside the solenoid is connected by straight lines that are **perpendicular to the axis** of the solenoid.
 
• This suggests that the** magnetic field **is **constant** (i.e., the exact same at every position inside the solenoid) inside the device.
 
• Electromagnets are created using the magnetic field of a current-carrying solenoid.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6abf70c603031349d3b82f1ea30656d590d4bf7abb4eb1fabeed984739b3dc0d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **electromagnet** known as a **solenoid** creates a regulated magnetic field using a helical coil of wire whose length is significantly higher than its diameter.
 
• When an electric **current **is run through the** coil**, it can create a consistent magnetic field inside a defined region of space.
 
• A solenoid's** helical** coil does not always have to circle around an axis that is in a **straight line**.
